chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a female slave who had been manumitted upon death (mudabbarah) and had run away (abqa) from her master for years, then she returned after her master had died, bringing with her many children and possessions. Two witnesses testified that her master had indeed manumitted her upon death while he was alive, before she ran away. He said: 'I see that she and all that is with her belongs to the heirs.' I said: 'Will she not be manumitted from one-third of her master's estate?' He said: 'No, for she ran away while disobedient to Allah, Exalted and Majestic, and to her master, and the running away (ibaq) annulled the manumission (tadbir).'

key_terms.مُدَبَّرَةٍ: A slave designated for manumission upon the master's death

ai.seo_question: What happens to a mudabbarah slave who runs away before her master dies?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rules that a female slave designated for manumission (mudabbarah) who runs away (abqa) before her master's death forfeits her freedom, as her disobedience annuls the tadbir. Consequently, she and her offspring revert to being part of the master's estate and belong to his heirs, rather than being freed from a third of his wealth. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the condition of 'abqa' (running away) acts as a revocation of the manumission contract due to the slave's breach of duty.
